title: 是 (shì) — To Be
explanation: 是 (shì) is the verb 'to be'. It links a subject to a noun or noun phrase. Unlike English, 是 is NOT used before adjectives — use 很 instead.
notes: Don't say 天气是好 ✗. Use 天气很好 ✓. 是 is only for nouns, not adjectives.

title: 不是 (bú shì) — Negative 'To Be'
explanation: Place 不 before 是 to negate it. 不 (bù) becomes bú before a 4th-tone syllable in speech, but the character stays 不 in writing.

examples.pinyin: Zhè bú shì wǒ de shū.

title: 有 / 没有 — Have / Don't Have
explanation: 有 (yǒu) means 'have' or 'there is/are'. Its only negation is 没有 (méiyǒu) — never 不有. 有 also expresses existence.

examples.pinyin: Zhuōzi shàng yǒu yī běn shū.
examples.english: There is a book on the table.

notes: NEVER say 不有 ✗ — the negation of 有 is always 没有.

title: 很 + Adjective — Predicate Adjectives
explanation: Adjectives in Chinese can be predicates without 是. They are usually preceded by 很 (hěn). In this position 很 is often grammatically required rather than meaning 'very'.

examples.pinyin: Zhè běn shū hěn yǒu yìsi.

notes: Omitting 很 implies a comparison: 今天天气好 can mean 'today's weather is good (compared to yesterday)'.

title: 的 (de) — Possessive / Attributive
explanation: 的 (de) marks possession (like 's in English) and links adjectives or clauses to nouns.
notes: With close relationships 的 can be dropped: 我妈妈 is natural for 'my mum'.

title: 吗 (ma) — Yes/No Questions
explanation: Add 吗 to the end of any statement to make it a yes/no question. No word-order change is needed.

title: 不 (bù) — Negation
explanation: 不 negates verbs and adjectives in the present/future or for general statements. For past actions, use 没 instead.

examples.pinyin: Tā bú shì wǒ de péngyǒu.

notes: Use 没 for past actions: 我没去 ✓ (I didn't go). 不 is for habit, present, and future.

title: 也 (yě) — Also / Too
explanation: 也 means 'also' or 'too' and always comes BEFORE the verb — never at the end of a sentence.
notes: 我也去 ✓ (I'm also going). NOT 我去也 ✗ — 也 goes before the verb, not after.

title: 都 (dōu) — All / Both
explanation: 都 means 'all' or 'both' and must come BEFORE the verb. The subject it refers to must precede 都.

examples.english: Both she and I are going.

notes: 他们都来了 ✓, not 都他们来了 ✗ — the subject must come first.

title: 在 (zài) — Location
explanation: 在 marks location ('be at / in'). It can also act as a preposition before a verb phrase: 我在北京工作 (I work in Beijing).

examples.english: The book is on the table.

title: 了 (le) — Completion
explanation: 了 after a verb marks a completed action. It is about completion, not strictly past tense — a future action can also be 'completed'.
notes: 了 at sentence-end can also signal a change of state: 他来了 means 'He has arrived (he wasn't here before)'.

title: Measure Words (量词 liàngcí)
explanation: A measure word must sit between a number and a noun. Different nouns require different measure words. 个 (gè) is the most common and works as a fallback.

examples.english: one cup of tea (杯 for cups)
five sheets of paper (张 for flat things)

notes: Use 两 (liǎng) not 二 (èr) before measure words: 两个 ✓, 二个 ✗.

title: 想 (xiǎng) — Want To
explanation: 想 before a verb expresses desire: 'want to' or 'would like to'. It is a modal verb followed directly by another verb.

examples.english: I want to go to Beijing.
What do you want to eat?

title: 能 vs 会 — Two Ways to Say 'Can'
explanation: Both mean 'can' but differ: 会 (huì) = learned skill (know how to); 能 (néng) = circumstantial or physical ability (be able to in this situation).

examples.english: Can you help me? (is it possible?)

notes: If you learned it → 会. If it depends on the situation or physical possibility → 能.

title: Time Word Position
pattern: Time + Subject + Verb  OR  Subject + Time + Verb
explanation: Time words in Chinese are flexible — they go at the sentence start or after the subject. They can NEVER go after the verb.

examples.english: Tomorrow he'll come to my home.

notes: 我去学校今天 ✗ — time words cannot go at the end of a sentence.

title: 比 (bǐ) — Comparison
explanation: 比 compares two things. The adjective describes A relative to B. Do NOT use 很 before the adjective in a 比 sentence.
notes: 他比我很高 ✗ — no 很 in comparisons. For 'much taller' say 他比我高多了.

title: 从...到... — From...To...
explanation: 从 (cóng) means 'from' and 到 (dào) means 'to'. Together they express a range of place, time, or amount.

examples.pinyin: Cóng Běijīng dào Shànghǎi hěn yuǎn.
examples.english: From Beijing to Shanghai is very far.

examples.chinese: 我从早上八点到下午五点工作。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ cóng zǎoshang bā diǎn dào xiàwǔ wǔ diǎn gōngzuò.
examples.english: I work from 8 am to 5 pm.

title: 因为...所以... — Because...Therefore...
explanation: 因为 (yīnwèi) = 'because', 所以 (suǒyǐ) = 'therefore / so'. In Chinese both halves are often stated together, unlike English where you only use one.

examples.pinyin: Yīnwèi xià yǔ, suǒyǐ wǒ bù qù.
examples.english: Because it's raining, I won't go.

examples.chinese: 因为我很忙，所以我没来。
examples.pinyin: Yīnwèi wǒ hěn máng, suǒyǐ wǒ méi lái.
examples.english: Because I was busy, I didn't come.

notes: You can use either word alone, but using both is the most natural pattern.

title: 但是 (dànshì) — But / However
explanation: 但是 connects two contrasting ideas. The shorter 但 (dàn) is also common, especially in writing.

examples.pinyin: Tā hěn máng, dànshì hěn gāoxìng.
examples.english: He is very busy, but very happy.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng qù, dànshì méiyǒu shíjiān.
examples.english: I want to go, but I don't have time.

title: 一边...一边... — Doing Two Things at Once
pattern: Subject + 一边 + Verb1，一边 + Verb2
explanation: 一边...一边... expresses two simultaneous actions: 'while doing X, also doing Y'. Both verbs should be ongoing activities.

examples.chinese: 他一边吃饭，一边看电视。
examples.pinyin: Tā yībiān chīfàn, yībiān kàn diànshì.

examples.chinese: 我喜欢一边听音乐，一边学习。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuān yībiān tīng yīnyuè, yībiān xuéxí.
examples.english: I like studying while listening to music.

title: 正在 (zhèngzài) — Progressive
explanation: 正在 marks an action in progress right now, like the English '-ing' form. 呢 can optionally follow for extra emphasis.

title: 先...然后... — First...Then...
explanation: 先 (xiān) = 'first', 然后 (ránhòu) = 'then / afterwards'. Together they sequence two actions.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiān chīfàn, ránhòu qù xuéxiào.
examples.english: I'll eat first, then go to school.

examples.pinyin: Xiān xiě zuòyè, ránhòu kàn diànshì.
examples.english: Do homework first, then watch TV.

title: 还是 (háishi) — Or (in Questions)
explanation: 还是 is used in choice questions ('A or B?'). It is different from 或者 (huòzhě), which is 'or' in statements.

examples.english: Do you drink tea or coffee?
Are you going to Beijing or Shanghai?

notes: 还是 = 'or' in questions. 或者 = 'or' in statements. Don't mix them up.
